  - id: C2
    label: "Symbolic Confirmation Bias as Root Cause (CORE)"
    status: VERIFIED
    internal_claims: [C7_new]
    claim: >
      Self-extracted FOL constraints systematically confirm the trace's
      own (possibly incorrect) answer rather than independently verifying
      ground truth. On SICA-incorrect problems, 83.3% of constraints
      support the wrong answer (bias ratio 4.97×). 94% of SICA errors
      overlap with SC errors (registry: sica_errors_follow_sc=0.94). The 12 SICA-correct flips come from minority
      trace diversity (43% gold support), not symbolic reasoning. Oracle
      gold-FOL proves aggregation is sound (+14.22pp FOLIO, +11.50pp PW,
      p<0.001); self-extraction captures only 24% of this ceiling. The
      causal chain: model reasons → answer → FOL extraction confirms
      answer → aggregation ≈ SC.
    evidence: "§5.2, §4.3 (Oracle), Table 1 oracle rows"
    registry_refs:
      - exp-confirmation-bias
      - exp-031  # Oracle FOLIO
      - exp-022  # Oracle PW
      - exp-direction-d-cegis  # CEGIS validates: consistency ≠ bottleneck

  - id: C3
    label: "Process-κ Reveals Deeper Independence Bottleneck (NEW METRIC)"
    status: VERIFIED
    internal_claims: [C8_new, C1_old]
    claim: >
      Answer-level κ underestimates the true independence bottleneck.
      CoT reasoning similarity (cosine=0.69) far exceeds answer-κ (0.41),
      with near-zero correlation (r=-0.06, p=0.36). Only 9.3% of trace
      pairs exhibit convergent reasoning (same answer, different process).
      This metric generalizes beyond SICA to all LLM trace aggregation
      methods. Combined with answer-κ quantification: Fleiss' κ=0.21–0.82
      (Eff-K=1.20–3.62 at K=12) across 15 conditions; three model families
      all produce κ≥0.41, confirming universality.
    evidence: "§3.4 (definition), §5.3 (results), Table 3"
    registry_refs:
      - exp-wild4-process-kappa
      - exp-cross-model-phase1  # Cross-model κ

  - id: C4
    label: "Regime-Dependent Pattern and Zero-Cost Diagnostics"
    status: VERIFIED
    internal_claims: [C3_old, C5_old]
    claim: >
      SICA effectiveness depends sharply on SC accuracy regime. A
      directional positive trend (best +3.43pp, mean +1.47pp; 0/4 seeds
      significant) appears only in a narrow band (~50–55% SC) on one model.
      Three failure modes: confirmation bias (Type A, SC≥60%), non-
      formalizability (Type B), error amplification (Type C, SC≤40%).
      C0 combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost deployment
      diagnostic. Entropy decomposition confirms: all SICA effects
      concentrate in high-entropy problems; direction depends on regime.
    evidence: "Table 1, Figure 2, §4.1–4.4, Appendix entropy"
    registry_refs:
      - exp-033  # Mistral FOLIO s42 (hero)
      - exp-052  # s123
      - exp-053  # s456

      - exp-046  # Type C

1	Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces saturates as sample count grows because same-model traces are correlated voters.
2	We investigate whether symbolic constraint extraction can break this plateau through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts first-order logic (FOL) constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT.
3	Evaluating six models (7B--32B) across three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances, we find that self-extracted constraints fail to surpass majority voting: none of fifteen non-degenerate conditions shows a significant positive effect ($p < 0.05$), while two conditions show significant degradation.
4	We identify \emph{symbolic confirmation bias} as the root cause: on incorrect problems, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratio $4.97\times$), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC.
5	Process-level analysis reveals a deeper bottleneck: chain-of-thought cosine similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level Fleiss' $\kappa$ ($0.41$), indicating that traces share reasoning processes even when they diverge on answers.
6	More than twenty-five same-model remediation strategies---spanning prompt engineering, method-level redesign, and ten additional directions---all fail, revealing a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off: methods that increase trace independence destroy accuracy (Debate: $\kappa = 0.15$, $-18.6$\,pp), while methods preserving accuracy cannot break the correlation floor ($\kappa \geq 0.40$ across three model families).
7	Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+11.50$\,pp ProofWriter, $p < 0.001$); self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling.
8	However, a cross-architecture proof-of-concept---DeBERTa-small NLI combined with SC---achieves $+3.43$\,pp through per-label complementarity, demonstrating that the oracle gap is practically recoverable when verification signal comes from outside the reasoning model's distribution.

Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces saturates as sample count grows because same-model traces are correlated voters.
We investigate whether symbolic constraint extraction can break this plateau through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts first-order logic (FOL) constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT.
Evaluating six models (7B--32B) across three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances, we find that self-extracted constraints fail to surpass majority voting: none of fifteen non-degenerate conditions shows a significant positive effect ($p < 0.05$), while two conditions show significant degradation.
We identify \emph{symbolic confirmation bias} as the root cause: on incorrect problems, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratio $4.97\times$), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC.
Process-level analysis reveals a deeper bottleneck: chain-of-thought cosine similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level Fleiss' $\kappa$ ($0.41$), indicating that traces share reasoning processes even when they diverge on answers.
More than twenty-five same-model remediation strategies---spanning prompt engineering, method-level redesign, and ten additional directions---all fail, revealing a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off: methods that increase trace independence destroy accuracy (Debate: $\kappa = 0.15$, $-18.6$\,pp), while methods preserving accuracy cannot break the correlation floor ($\kappa \geq 0.40$ across three model families).
Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+11.50$\,pp ProofWriter, $p < 0.001$); self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling.
However, a cross-architecture proof-of-concept---DeBERTa-small NLI combined with SC---achieves $+3.43$\,pp through per-label complementarity, demonstrating that the oracle gap is practically recoverable when verification signal comes from outside the reasoning model's distribution.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces saturates as sample count grows because same-model traces are correlated voters.
We investigate whether symbolic constraint extraction can break this plateau through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts first-order logic (FOL) constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT.
Evaluating six models (7B--32B) across three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances, we find that self-extracted constraints fail to surpass majority voting: none of fifteen non-degenerate conditions shows a significant positive effect ($p < 0.05$), while two conditions show significant degradation.
We identify \emph{symbolic confirmation bias} as the root cause: on incorrect problems, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratio $4.97\times$), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC.
Process-level analysis reveals a deeper bottleneck: chain-of-thought cosine similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level Fleiss' $\kappa$ ($0.41$), indicating that traces share reasoning processes even when they diverge on answers.
More than twenty-five same-model remediation strategies---spanning prompt engineering, method-level redesign, and ten additional directions---all fail, revealing a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off: methods that increase trace independence destroy accuracy (Debate: $\kappa = 0.15$, $-18.6$\,pp), while methods preserving accuracy cannot break the correlation floor ($\kappa \geq 0.40$ across three model families).
Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+11.50$\,pp ProofWriter, $p < 0.001$); self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling.
However, a cross-architecture proof-of-concept---DeBERTa-small NLI combined with SC---achieves $+3.43$\,pp through per-label complementarity, demonstrating that the oracle gap is practically recoverable when verification signal comes from outside the reasoning model's distribution.

Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces saturates as sample count grows because same-model traces are correlated voters.
We investigate whether symbolic constraint extraction can break this plateau through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts first-order logic (FOL) constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT.
Evaluating six models (7B--32B) across three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances, we find that self-extracted constraints fail to surpass majority voting: none of fifteen non-degenerate conditions shows a significant positive effect ($p < 0.05$), while two conditions show significant degradation.
We identify \emph{symbolic confirmation bias} as the root cause: on incorrect problems, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratio $4.97\times$), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC.
Process-level analysis reveals a deeper bottleneck: chain-of-thought cosine similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level Fleiss' $\kappa$ ($0.41$), indicating that traces share reasoning processes even when they diverge on answers.
More than twenty-five same-model remediation strategies---spanning prompt engineering, method-level redesign, and ten additional directions---all fail, revealing a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off: methods that increase trace independence destroy accuracy (Debate: $\kappa = 0.15$, $-18.6$\,pp), while methods preserving accuracy cannot break the correlation floor ($\kappa \geq 0.40$ across three model families).
Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+11.50$\,pp ProofWriter, $p < 0.001$); self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling.
However, a cross-architecture proof-of-concept---DeBERTa-large NLI combined with SC---achieves $+4.41$\,pp ($p = 0.039$) through per-label complementarity, demonstrating that the oracle gap is practically recoverable when verification signal comes from outside the reasoning model's distribution.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models on three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances. Beyond accuracy comparisons, we conduct diagnostic analyses of symbolic confirmation bias and process-level trace independence (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B parameters).

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n{=}204$, with gold FOL annotations), ProofWriter depth-5~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n{=}600$), LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n{=}200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n{=}200$) serves as a domain-formalizability diagnostic. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} ($n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$; extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$. Z3 timeout: 10s. $\alpha{=}0.5$. Statistical significance via McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs from 10,000 resamples for $n \geq 200$.


\subsection{Main Results}
\label{sec:main-results}

Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports accuracy across all conditions sorted by SC baseline. SICA effectiveness depends sharply on the accuracy regime.

\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{SICA vs.\ SC across all conditions sorted by SC accuracy. $\Delta$ = SICA $-$ SC (pp). $^b$In-context learning with gold FOL examples. $\dagger$\,$n < 100$ (suggestive only). \textbf{Bold $\Delta$}: $p < 0.05$ (McNemar). {*}\,$p < 0.05$;\enspace{**}\,$p < 0.01$;\enspace{***}\,$p < 0.001$. Failure modes detailed in Appendix~\ref{app:failure-modes}.}
\label{tab:main_results}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llrrrrl@{}}
\toprule
Model & Domain & $n$ & SC (\%) & SICA (\%) & $\Delta$ (pp) & $p$ \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type C: error amplification (SC $\leq$ 40\%)}} \\
Mistral-7B & PW-D5 & 600 & 39.33 & 36.50 & $\mathbf{-2.83}$ & 0.014{*} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Intermediate SC (SC $\sim$50--55\%, Mistral-7B only)}} \\
Mistral-7B & LogiQA & 200 & 51.00 & 51.50 & $+$0.50 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s123) & 204 & 54.41 & 57.35 & $+$2.94 & 0.070 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s42) & 204 & 55.88 & \textbf{59.31} & $+$3.43 & 0.092 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s456) & 204 & 55.88 & 55.88 & 0.00 & 1.000 \\
Mistral-7B & FOLIO (s789) & 204 & 54.41 & 53.92 & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Type A: confirmation bias (SC $\geq$ 60\%)}} \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & FOLIO & 204 & 66.18 & 61.76 & $-$4.41 & 0.093 \\
LLaMA-3.1-8B & StrategyQA & 200 & 72.00 & 74.00 & $+$2.00 & 0.424 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO (ICL)$^b$ & 199 & 74.37 & 74.87 & $+$0.50 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 75.17 & 72.67 & $\mathbf{-2.50}$ & 0.011{*} \\
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.49 & 74.51 & $-$0.98 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-7B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.98 & 76.47 & $+$0.49 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-14B & LogiQA & 200 & 78.50 & 78.00 & $-$0.50 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 84.80 & \textbf{84.31} & $-$0.49 & 1.000 \\
Qwen3-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 85.00 & 85.67 & $+$0.67 & 1.000 \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Degenerate ($C_0 < 5\%$)}} \\
QwQ-32B & AIME 2024$^\dagger$ & 22 & 72.70 & 72.70 & 0.00 & \textrm{---} \\
Qwen2.5-14B & GSM8K$^\dagger$ & 30 & 96.67 & 96.67 & 0.00 & \textrm{---} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Oracle upper bound (gold FOL/DSL + Z3)}} \\
Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.49 & \textbf{89.71} & $\mathbf{+14.22}$ & $2.0{\times}10^{-7}${***} \\
Qwen2.5-14B & ProofWriter & 600 & 75.17 & \textbf{86.67} & $\mathbf{+11.50}$ & $9.21{\times}10^{-15}${***} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}

\paragraph{Intermediate-SC region.} Mistral-7B on FOLIO (SC $\sim$50--55\%) shows positive directional trends in 2 of 4 seeds: $\Delta = +3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.092$) and $+2.94$\,pp ($p = 0.070$); the remaining seeds show null or negative results. No seed reaches $p < 0.05$; the 4-seed mean is $+1.47$\,pp. Mistral-7B on LogiQA, despite the same SC range, yields only $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp ($p = 1.0$), attributable to domain formalizability (Appendix~\ref{app:failure-modes}).

\paragraph{Type A (SC $\geq$ 60\%): confirmation bias.} Nine conditions with SC $\geq 63\%$ (combined $N > 2{,}800$) produce no significant positive effects. Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter shows significant degradation ($\Delta = -2.50$\,pp, $p = 0.011$). Even in-context learning with gold FOL examples ($\Delta = +0.50$\,pp, n.s.) cannot break confirmation bias.

\paragraph{Type C (SC $\leq$ 40\%): error amplification.} Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($n = 600$, SC $= 39.33\%$) shows $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.014$): SICA \emph{significantly hurts} by formalizing incorrect reasoning.

\paragraph{Degenerate cases.} When $C_0 < 5\%$, nearly all traces agree and SICA reduces to SC by construction.

Figure~\ref{fig:regime-scatter} visualizes the regime dependence: the intermediate-SC region is narrow and observed only for Mistral-7B on FOLIO.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{f2_regime_scatter}
\caption{SICA $\Delta$ (pp) vs.\ SC baseline. Filled: $n \geq 100$; open: $n < 100$. The intermediate-SC region (50--55\%, shaded) contains the only positive trends (none reaching $p < 0.05$). Type~C: significant degradation ($p = 0.014$).}
\label{fig:regime-scatter}
\end{figure}


\subsection{Oracle Control}
\label{sec:oracle}

Oracle variants replace self-extracted constraints with gold annotations: FOL from FOLIO ($n = 204$) and DSL from ProofWriter ($n = 600$). Oracle-SICA achieves 89.71\% on FOLIO ($\Delta = +14.22$\,pp, $p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$) and 86.67\% on ProofWriter ($\Delta = +11.50$\,pp, $p = 9.21 \times 10^{-15}$). Z3 agrees with gold labels on 95.1\% (FOLIO) and 97.1\% (ProofWriter) of problems.

These results establish that the MAX-SAT mechanism is sound given discriminative constraints. Mistral-7B's best self-extracted result ($+3.43$\,pp) captures only 24.1\% of the FOLIO oracle ceiling. The remaining 75.9\% is lost to self-extraction quality.


\subsection{Cross-Architecture Verification}
\label{sec:cross-arch}

The oracle gap motivates testing whether external signal can help in practice.
DeBERTa-v3-small NLI (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch-method}) provides a cross-architecture verification signal on Mistral-7B FOLIO ($n = 204$, seed~123).

DeBERTa NLI alone achieves 49.51\% (below SC's 54.41\%), but \emph{combo} mode (NLI + SC, $w{=}3$) reaches 57.84\% ($\Delta = +3.43$\,pp).
Per-label analysis reveals complementary strengths: NLI improves on \textsc{False} by $+33$\,pp over SC, while SC dominates on \textsc{Unknown} by $+49$\,pp.
This $+3.43$\,pp gain derives from architectural complementarity rather than same-model constraint extraction.
While preliminary (single seed, one dataset), the result provides proof-of-concept that the oracle gap is practically recoverable through cross-architecture verification \citep{xu2026dylos, wang2025fover}.


\subsection{Four-Seed Replication}
\label{sec:replication}

Four seeds on Mistral-7B FOLIO ($n = 204$, $K = 12$, $T = 0.7$) yield $\Delta$ from $+3.43$ to $-0.49$\,pp (mean $+1.47$\,pp); 2 of 4 show marginal trends ($p < 0.10$), none reaches $p < 0.05$. Seeds~42 and~456 share identical SC baselines (55.88\%) yet diverge ($+3.43$ vs.\ $0.00$\,pp), indicating seed-level constraint quality---not SC level alone---drives the effect (entropy decomposition in Appendix~\ref{app:entropy}).

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

We evaluated SICA across six models (three families), three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 instances. The root cause of failure is symbolic confirmation bias: on incorrect problems, 83.3\% of constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratio $4.97\times$), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC. Process-level similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level $\kappa$ ($0.41$), and twenty-five+ same-model remediation strategies all fail to escape the independence-accuracy Pareto frontier ($\kappa \geq 0.40$). A cross-architecture proof-of-concept---DeBERTa-small NLI combined with SC---achieves $+3.43$\,pp, providing preliminary evidence that the oracle gap is practically recoverable through external verification. For practitioners, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost deployment diagnostic; when the independence bottleneck binds, cross-architecture verifiers offer an actionable path forward.

1	\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
2	
3	Test-time computation scaling through multiple reasoning samples has emerged as a practical alternative to scaling model parameters \citep{snell2025scaling, guo2025deepseekr1}.
4	The dominant aggregation strategy, Self-Consistency (SC) \citep{wang2023sc}, samples $K$ chain-of-thought traces and selects the majority answer.
5	SC is simple, model-agnostic, and effective---but it is hitting a ceiling.
6	\citet{loo2025reevaluating} demonstrate that gains from increasing $K$ plateau and even decline for strong models.
7	The gap between SC's theoretical promise (independent correct voters converge to truth) and its practical behavior (saturating gains) points to a structural mismatch: same-model traces carry correlated errors, and majority voting has no mechanism to correct shared bias.
8	
9	Confidence-weighted \citep{taubenfeld2025cisc} and universal \citep{chen2024usc} extensions alleviate this to a degree, but the core limitation persists.
10	Recent neuro-symbolic methods---Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}, LINC \citep{olausson2023linc}, DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, LogicAgent \citep{luo2025logicagent}---each report gains on logical reasoning, but introduce components beyond the reasoning model: trained verifiers, solver selection, or external knowledge.
11	A simpler question precedes these: can the \emph{same} model that generates reasoning traces also extract useful formal constraints from them?
12	Self-extraction would be a zero-cost upgrade requiring no additional model, training data, or external prover.
13	Yet no prior work has systematically evaluated whether self-extracted constraints are useful for aggregation.
14	
15	We ground our analysis in the Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) \citep{condorcet1785}: if $K$ independent voters each answer correctly with probability $p > 0.5$, the majority converges to truth \citep{austensmith1996}.
16	When independence fails \citep{ladha1992correlated}, additional samples carry diminishing information.
17	Measuring inter-trace agreement with Fleiss' $\kappa$ \citep{fleiss1971kappa}, we find $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ across instruction-tuned conditions, yielding Effective-$K = 1.20$--$3.62$ for nominal $K = 12$: traces beyond a dozen add negligible independent information (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}).

21	Self-extraction cannot supply the independent signal that CJT requires.
22	
23	We study this through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA): extract FOL constraints from each of $K$ reasoning traces, deduplicate by syntactic equivalence, and select the answer best supported by a weighted partial MAX-SAT solution via Z3 \citep{demoura2008z3} (\S\ref{sec:pipeline}; Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
24	We evaluate SICA across six models (7B--32B), three reasoning domains (FOLIO \citep{han2022folio}, ProofWriter \citep{tafjord2021proofwriter}, LogiQA \citep{liu2020logiqa}), and over 3,000 instances with four-seed replication (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}).
25	More than twenty-five remediation strategies---spanning prompt engineering, method-level redesign, and ten additional directions targeting the independence bottleneck---all produce neutral or negative results, confirming the bottleneck is structural at the 7B--32B scale tested.
26	
27	Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound: gold FOL yields $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling (\S\ref{sec:oracle}).

29	A cross-architecture proof-of-concept demonstrates that this gap is recoverable: DeBERTa-small NLI combined with SC achieves $+3.43$\,pp through per-label complementarity (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}).
30	
31	Our contributions are:

33	\item \textbf{Independence-Accuracy Trade-off.} Fleiss' $\kappa$ across four aggregation methods and three model families reveals a same-model Pareto frontier ($\kappa \geq 0.40$). Twenty-five+ remediation strategies fail; a cross-architecture NLI verifier provides proof-of-concept that the frontier is escapable (\S\ref{sec:remediation}, \S\ref{sec:cross-arch}).
34	
35	\item \textbf{Symbolic Confirmation Bias.} On incorrect problems, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratio $4.97\times$), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}).
36	
37	\item \textbf{Process-Level Independence.} CoT cosine similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level $\kappa$ ($0.41$), showing reasoning processes are more homogeneous than answer distributions suggest (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}, \S\ref{sec:process-kappa}).
38

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Test-time computation scaling through multiple reasoning samples has emerged as a practical alternative to scaling model parameters \citep{snell2025scaling, guo2025deepseekr1}.
The dominant aggregation strategy, Self-Consistency (SC) \citep{wang2023sc}, samples $K$ chain-of-thought traces and selects the majority answer.
SC is simple, model-agnostic, and effective---but it is hitting a ceiling.
\citet{loo2025reevaluating} demonstrate that gains from increasing $K$ plateau and even decline for strong models.
The gap between SC's theoretical promise (independent correct voters converge to truth) and its practical behavior (saturating gains) points to a structural mismatch: same-model traces carry correlated errors, and majority voting has no mechanism to correct shared bias.

Confidence-weighted \citep{taubenfeld2025cisc} and universal \citep{chen2024usc} extensions alleviate this to a degree, but the core limitation persists.
Recent neuro-symbolic methods---Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}, LINC \citep{olausson2023linc}, DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, LogicAgent \citep{luo2025logicagent}---each report gains on logical reasoning, but introduce components beyond the reasoning model: trained verifiers, solver selection, or external knowledge.
A simpler question precedes these: can the \emph{same} model that generates reasoning traces also extract useful formal constraints from them?
Self-extraction would be a zero-cost upgrade requiring no additional model, training data, or external prover.
Yet no prior work has systematically evaluated whether self-extracted constraints are useful for aggregation.

We ground our analysis in the Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) \citep{condorcet1785}: if $K$ independent voters each answer correctly with probability $p > 0.5$, the majority converges to truth \citep{austensmith1996}.
When independence fails \citep{ladha1992correlated}, additional samples carry diminishing information.
Measuring inter-trace agreement with Fleiss' $\kappa$ \citep{fleiss1971kappa}, we find $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ across instruction-tuned conditions, yielding Effective-$K = 1.20$--$3.62$ for nominal $K = 12$: traces beyond a dozen add negligible independent information (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}).
The bottleneck runs deeper than answer-level agreement suggests.
Chain-of-thought cosine similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level $\kappa$ ($0.41$), revealing that traces share reasoning processes even when they diverge on final answers (\S\ref{sec:process-kappa}).
When the same model extracts FOL constraints from these correlated traces, the constraints exhibit \emph{symbolic confirmation bias}: on problems where the model errs, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratio $4.97\times$), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}).
Self-extraction cannot supply the independent signal that CJT requires.

We study this through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA): extract FOL constraints from each of $K$ reasoning traces, deduplicate by syntactic equivalence, and select the answer best supported by a weighted partial MAX-SAT solution via Z3 \citep{demoura2008z3} (\S\ref{sec:pipeline}; Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
We evaluate SICA across six models (7B--32B), three reasoning domains (FOLIO \citep{han2022folio}, ProofWriter \citep{tafjord2021proofwriter}, LogiQA \citep{liu2020logiqa}), and over 3,000 instances with four-seed replication (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}).
More than twenty-five remediation strategies---spanning prompt engineering, method-level redesign, and ten additional directions targeting the independence bottleneck---all produce neutral or negative results, confirming the bottleneck is structural at the 7B--32B scale tested.

Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound: gold FOL yields $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling (\S\ref{sec:oracle}).
The central finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off: Debate reduces $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15 (tripling Eff-$K$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp; SC, Diverse-Prompt, and ICG all cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$, forming a same-model ceiling that holds across three model families (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
A cross-architecture proof-of-concept demonstrates that this gap is recoverable: DeBERTa-small NLI combined with SC achieves $+3.43$\,pp through per-label complementarity (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}).

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
\item \textbf{Independence-Accuracy Trade-off.} Fleiss' $\kappa$ across four aggregation methods and three model families reveals a same-model Pareto frontier ($\kappa \geq 0.40$). Twenty-five+ remediation strategies fail; a cross-architecture NLI verifier provides proof-of-concept that the frontier is escapable (\S\ref{sec:remediation}, \S\ref{sec:cross-arch}).

\item \textbf{Symbolic Confirmation Bias.} On incorrect problems, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratio $4.97\times$), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}).

\item \textbf{Process-Level Independence.} CoT cosine similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level $\kappa$ ($0.41$), showing reasoning processes are more homogeneous than answer distributions suggest (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}, \S\ref{sec:process-kappa}).

\item \textbf{Regime-Dependent Diagnostics.} Three failure modes create regime boundaries; $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost diagnostic predicting when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help (\S\ref{sec:main-results}).
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Unifying root cause.}

-Symbolic confirmation bias unifies two channels through which trace correlation degrades SICA: the \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity (Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions); the \emph{indirect} channel produces homogeneous constraints that cause MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting. Both stem from the same mechanism: the model generates an answer, then extracts FOL consistent with it. More than twenty-five same-model remediation strategies fail because each addresses a symptom rather than this root cause. The cross-architecture NLI experiment (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}) corroborates this: a 44M-parameter DeBERTa model provides the complementary signal that same-model methods cannot.

\paragraph{Practitioner implications.}

$C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Process-level similarity ($0.69$) exceeding answer-level $\kappa$ ($0.41$) implies that interventions spreading answers may still fail to diversify reasoning. Published systems reporting positive results \citep{xu2026dylos, li2025aristotle, wang2025fover, pan2023logiclm} each bypass same-model self-extraction, consistent with our diagnosis.

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

We evaluated SICA across six models (three families), three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 instances. The root cause of failure is symbolic confirmation bias: on incorrect problems, 83.3\% of constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratio $4.97\times$), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC. Process-level similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level $\kappa$ ($0.41$), and twenty-five+ same-model remediation strategies all fail to escape the independence-accuracy Pareto frontier ($\kappa \geq 0.40$). A cross-architecture proof-of-concept---DeBERTa-small NLI combined with SC---achieves $+3.43$\,pp, providing preliminary evidence that the oracle gap is practically recoverable through external verification. For practitioners, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost deployment diagnostic; when the independence bottleneck binds, cross-architecture verifiers offer an actionable path forward.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models on three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances. Beyond accuracy comparisons, we conduct diagnostic analyses of symbolic confirmation bias and process-level trace independence (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B parameters).

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n{=}204$, with gold FOL annotations), ProofWriter depth-5~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n{=}600$), LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n{=}200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n{=}200$) serves as a domain-formalizability diagnostic. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} ($n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$; extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$. Z3 timeout: 10s. $\alpha{=}0.5$. Statistical significance via McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs from 10,000 resamples for $n \geq 200$.

\label{sec:main-results}

Qwen2.5-14B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.49 & 74.51 & $-$0.98 & 1.000 \\
Qwen2.5-7B & FOLIO & 204 & 75.98 & 76.47 & $+$0.49 & 1.000 \\

Qwen3-14B & PW-D5 & 600 & 85.00 & 85.67 & $+$0.67 & 1.000 \\

\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Degenerate ($C_0 < 5\%$)}} \\

\midrule
\multicolumn{7}{l}{\textit{Oracle upper bound (gold FOL/DSL + Z3)}} \\

\paragraph{Intermediate-SC region.} Mistral-7B on FOLIO (SC $\sim$50--55\%) shows positive directional trends in 2 of 4 seeds: $\Delta = +3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.092$) and $+2.94$\,pp ($p = 0.070$); the remaining seeds show null or negative results. No seed reaches $p < 0.05$; the 4-seed mean is $+1.47$\,pp. Mistral-7B on LogiQA, despite the same SC range, yields only $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp ($p = 1.0$), attributable to domain formalizability (Appendix~\ref{app:failure-modes}).

\paragraph{Type A (SC $\geq$ 60\%): confirmation bias.} Nine conditions with SC $\geq 63\%$ (combined $N > 2{,}800$) produce no significant positive effects. Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter shows significant degradation ($\Delta = -2.50$\,pp, $p = 0.011$). Even in-context learning with gold FOL examples ($\Delta = +0.50$\,pp, n.s.) cannot break confirmation bias.

\paragraph{Type C (SC $\leq$ 40\%): error amplification.} Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($n = 600$, SC $= 39.33\%$) shows $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.014$): SICA \emph{significantly hurts} by formalizing incorrect reasoning.

\paragraph{Degenerate cases.} When $C_0 < 5\%$, nearly all traces agree and SICA reduces to SC by construction.

Figure~\ref{fig:regime-scatter} visualizes the regime dependence: the intermediate-SC region is narrow and observed only for Mistral-7B on FOLIO.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{f2_regime_scatter}
\caption{SICA $\Delta$ (pp) vs.\ SC baseline. Filled: $n \geq 100$; open: $n < 100$. The intermediate-SC region (50--55\%, shaded) contains the only positive trends (none reaching $p < 0.05$). Type~C: significant degradation ($p = 0.014$).}
\label{fig:regime-scatter}
\end{figure}


\subsection{Oracle Control}
\label{sec:oracle}

Oracle variants replace self-extracted constraints with gold annotations: FOL from FOLIO ($n = 204$) and DSL from ProofWriter ($n = 600$). Oracle-SICA achieves 89.71\% on FOLIO ($\Delta = +14.22$\,pp, $p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$) and 86.67\% on ProofWriter ($\Delta = +11.50$\,pp, $p = 9.21 \times 10^{-15}$). Z3 agrees with gold labels on 95.1\% (FOLIO) and 97.1\% (ProofWriter) of problems.

These results establish that the MAX-SAT mechanism is sound given discriminative constraints. Mistral-7B's best self-extracted result ($+3.43$\,pp) captures only 24.1\% of the FOLIO oracle ceiling. The remaining 75.9\% is lost to self-extraction quality.


\subsection{Cross-Architecture Verification}
\label{sec:cross-arch}

The oracle gap motivates testing whether external signal can help in practice.
DeBERTa-v3-small NLI (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch-method}) provides a cross-architecture verification signal on Mistral-7B FOLIO ($n = 204$, seed~123).

DeBERTa NLI alone achieves 49.51\% (below SC's 54.41\%), but \emph{combo} mode (NLI + SC, $w{=}3$) reaches 57.84\% ($\Delta = +3.43$\,pp).
Per-label analysis reveals complementary strengths: NLI improves on \textsc{False} by $+33$\,pp over SC, while SC dominates on \textsc{Unknown} by $+49$\,pp.
This $+3.43$\,pp gain derives from architectural complementarity rather than same-model constraint extraction.
While preliminary (single seed, one dataset), the result provides proof-of-concept that the oracle gap is practically recoverable through cross-architecture verification \citep{xu2026dylos, wang2025fover}.


\subsection{Four-Seed Replication}
\label{sec:replication}

Four seeds on Mistral-7B FOLIO ($n = 204$, $K = 12$, $T = 0.7$) yield $\Delta$ from $+3.43$ to $-0.49$\,pp (mean $+1.47$\,pp); 2 of 4 show marginal trends ($p < 0.10$), none reaches $p < 0.05$. Seeds~42 and~456 share identical SC baselines (55.88\%) yet diverge ($+3.43$ vs.\ $0.00$\,pp), indicating seed-level constraint quality---not SC level alone---drives the effect (entropy decomposition in Appendix~\ref{app:entropy}).
